subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module using the builder API, with imports for joints, parts, rods, sweeps, extrusions, and lathe operations plus glow and paint helpers, aiming to keep it compact but functional.

I'm sketching a cyberpunk militarized truck design: a 5.5m chassis with wheel joints, turret yaw/pitch, hazard-stripe and neon decal textures, and panelled gunmetal paint with magenta, cyan, and yellow accents. I'm now building out the hull structure with sloped armor plates using extruded profiles anchored to a chassis joint.

Defining hull outline coordinates...

Working out the windshield as a thin rotated box, calculating its tilt angle so the glass surface slopes to match the slanting cab roofline at roughly 40 degrees from horizontal.

Then I'm planning a 6x6 military truck layout with six wheels, front two steerable, positioning them along the hull with proper arch clearance, and designing each wheel as a composite of tire, tread blocks, rim, hub, lugs, and a glowing neon ring accent.

Writing wheel geometry merge code...

I'm also planning additional details like neon underglow strips along the rockers and slit-style glowing headlights.

Beyond that I'm sketching out a whole set of vehicle accessories: a toothed ram bumper with hazard-striped texture, a roof turret with yaw/pitch twin autocannons and a glowing red sensor dome, plus a light bar, antenna, dish, and missile pods. For the bed I'm adding a ribbed cargo box, a drone landing pad decal, ammo crates, and glowing rear thrusters, along with side skirts, reactive armor bricks, and smoke launchers. For decals I'm thinking door emblems, hazard stripes, a cab HUD screen, a license plate, and stenciled text like "2077" and "UNIT 07."

Now I'm adding more detail with camera-pod mirrors, rivet rows, side cables and hoses, and a radar panel, while settling on five core textures -- hazard stripes, emblem, HUD screen, plate, and a cyber glyph strip. I'm working out how to place decal planes on each flat panel so they face the correct direction and read properly from either side, and building a custom dirt-weathering paint layer for the lower body.

Writing paint logic...

Writing geometry helpers...

Now I'm working out the turret placement relative to the cab and bed, figuring out where the pedestal and yaw joint should sit along the hull's length so the weapons sit properly over the cargo area behind the cab.

I'm laying out the turret mechanism itself — yaw and pitch joints with their rotation axes, barrel pairs with muzzle brakes and shrouds, an ammo box with a belt, and a sensor ball for targeting, plus thinking through where missile pods could attach along the bed sides.

Now I'm positioning missile pod boxes angled on the sides, checking clearance against the turret radius, then moving to design rear thrusters as lathed bell shapes with glowing discs, a spiked front ram bumper, and headlight slits set into the sloped nose of the hull.

I'm adding a hazard-striped plate to the bumper and a dark grille panel with glowing vertical slats, then checking ground clearance between the chassis pan and wheels, adjusting wheel hub positions outward slightly so they sit just outside the hull without clipping.

Now I'm placing fender boxes over each wheel with mud flaps behind, adding simple suspension details (axle rods and stacked-torus coil springs that stay static), and sketching side skirt plates with slats to fill the gaps between the wheels along the hull.

I'm also planning the cab's side door seams as thin dark panel lines, deciding emblem placement should actually go on the larger hull side surface rather than the small cab door area, positioning it around the mid-height z-offset.

I'm adding bolted armor plates on the hull sides and reworking the cab to be taller since the current proportions feel too squat, like an APC. I'm recalculating the windshield's outline and slope angle to get a militarized, slit-window look.

Now I'm placing roof details like a light bar, sensor dome, antenna whip, and dish, and working out the hull's top-front slope leading into the hood area.

I'm positioning ERA blocks and small vents along the hull top slope, adding mirror arms with camera pods on each side, and detailing the bed walls, ribs, rear gate with a hazard texture panel, and rear thrusters tucked below the deck near the tailgate.

Instead of a drone pad, I'm skipping the crate idea due to clearance conflicts with the turret base and cab, opting instead for cylindrical fuel/power canisters with glow bands mounted on the rear bed sides, plus a cyan underglow strip along the hull edges. Now I'm starting the wheel-building function with tread segments arrayed around the hub.

Still writing tread placement math...

Adding the armor disc cover and spoke merge...

Now I'm thinking through the joint hierarchy for the chassis and wheels—steer joints for the front hubs feeding into spin joints, though I need to reconcile the wheel geometry's X-axis orientation with the rig's default bone direction before settling on the spin joint vector.

I'm sketching out the SVG textures next, starting with a hazard-stripe pattern using diagonal yellow and black polygons for the warning markings.

I'm designing the remaining decals: an emblem with a hex shield and glowing cyan numerals, a radar-style screen texture, a license plate reading "2077-NX," and a glyph panel switched to ASCII text since CJK fonts may not render reliably. I'm also planning to apply these as flat side decals facing outward, letting the glow effect pick up each texture's own colors.

Now I'm sketching out the construction loop for the full model: emissive glow colors for parts, a partial dome sphere for the roof, an antenna whip spike, cable sweeps using a catmull spline helper, and missile pod geometry with tube-shaped barrel openings up front.

Positioning the turret and barrels next, I'm checking placement to make sure the forward-facing barrels don't collide with the cab roof given their length and height.

Keeping the turret at the bed position, I'm sizing the barrel rods, shroud cylinder, muzzle brake, receiver box, angled shield plate, and a small glowing sensor eye, plus a side ammo box. I'll finalize these dimensions and proceed to write the code.

Setting up small box and cylinder helper functions tied to the bone, then planning rivet rows along the hull sides using small spheres and armor plates per side.

Checking wheel positions against hull geometry to avoid overlap, I'm picking z-centers for the side armor plates so they sit above the wheels and clear the hub areas.

Still placing geometry... I'm positioning the hazard panel and plate on the tailgate, then sketching the tailgate box dimensions and the rear thruster bell as a lathe shape near the hull's rear face.

I also need to double-check that the wheels sit at y=0 and the tire treads only sink about 2% into the ground, which is acceptable, before finalizing the answer.
